## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. In this mode, an extension’s support declaration matters when the application imports it: if the extension has no explicit declaration of support for free threading, CPython issues a warning and enables the GIL.

The declaration mechanism differs depending on whether the extension uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization. In either case, declaring support signals compatibility with the free-threading runtime mode; it does not establish that the extension’s code is thread-safe. Making the code thread-safe is a separate responsibility.
